subject: Literature
title: Wallace Stevens and the Imagination
description: A 60-second lesson on Wallace Stevens and the Imagination.

hook.text: Wallace Stevens spent his entire career as an insurance executive and wrote poetry at his desk between claims.

buildup.text: His poems argue that the imagination is not a luxury but the force that makes reality bearable and meaningful.

discovery.text: Thirteen Ways of Looking at a Blackbird presents the same bird from thirteen perspectives, each a tiny philosophical world.

twist.text: His coworkers at Hartford Accident and Indemnity had no idea he was one of the greatest American poets alive.

climax.text: Stevens proved that poetry and ordinary life are not opposites but that one can quietly sustain the other.

punchline.text: America's greatest poet wrote between insurance claims.

quiz.question: What was Stevens's day job while writing his celebrated poetry?
options: He was a university professor of literature
He was an insurance executive at Hartford Accident and Indemnity
He was a newspaper editor in New York
